name: 2010-2016_Cadillac WWTP_District Compliance File.pdf
description: Compiled district compliance-file source preserved as a distinct record package. Page 5 is the January 12, 2016 City spill letter: American Waste's leachate driver reported an offloading release at 9:22 a.m.; the truck could hold up to 10,000 gallons, but the letter states only that less than that amount spilled and provides no measured load or spill volume. Page 71 preserves the February 3, 2011 inspection history stating that the equalization tank accepted hauled waste described as County Landfill leachate and that no screen or flow meter was apparent in that receiving area. Page 2 contains the January 7, 2016 DEQ notebook entry summarizing 2015 CBOD, TSS, ammonia and other exceedances; January 6–7 call notes with Jeff Dietlin; a reported black discharge and noncompliance; and a concern that NMS was not flagging DMR violations or exceedances. Page 23 contains Julie Lowe's October 16, 2015 note to file concerning Michigan Rubber: Hamid had left the Cadillac WWTP and Jeff Dietlin was temporarily replacing him; reported oil-and-grease issues were resolved; the city warned Michigan Rubber and other Haring Township-line dischargers that responsible facilities could be fined if the discharge continued; Michigan Rubber contributed less than half of the Haring Township lift-station loading; and the WWTP was sampling Michigan Rubber monthly and treating it as categorical pending correction of its SIU-only listing in the next annual report.

description: EGLE's June 10, 2026 Violation Notice VN-019184 concerning Cadillac WWTP's April 16-29 treatment bypass. EGLE states that approximately 16.369 million gallons of partially treated sewage reached the Clam River and that required agency, health-department and public notices were not completed within 24 hours. The notice asks Cadillac either to document that a reportable-discharge-scenario storm threshold was exceeded or to submit corrective action; it is a formal agency allegation, not a final disposition.

name: 2026-02-27 to 2026-07-07 - Cadillac Cyanide Messages Chronological Sequence.pdf
description: Twenty-four-page chronological agency, municipal, laboratory and industrial-user correspondence package concerning 2026 cyanide results. It records Cadillac's exceedance notifications and resampling, the City's identification of Cadillac Casting as the suspected contributing industrial user, a reported plant-weir result of 3.5 mg/L compared with the City's stated 4 µg/L local limit, and issuance and receipt of a notice of violation. Statements are attributed to their source messages; the compilation is not treated as an independent adjudication.

name: 2016-11-03 - N0358 Western Concrete On-Site Inspection.pdf
description: November 3, 2016 AQD inspection of the former Western Concrete site at 510 5th Street in Cadillac. The inspector records that the concrete operation had closed, its equipment was removed, the building was being used by AAR Mobility for pallet storage, and the air permits were to be voided. This is industrial-site history and does not by itself establish PFAS use or release.

name: 2022-06-29 - N3862 Wexford County Landfill On-Site Inspection.pdf
description: June 29, 2022 AQD inspection report for Wexford County Landfill. It documents the active landfill-gas collection and flare system, March 2022 NMOC testing at 32.33 Mg/year, continued compliance, and the inspector's statement that the 2018 deep-injection well ended leachate trucking and evaporation.

name: 2013-09-30 - Cadillac WWTP NPDES CEI Pre-Inspection Report.pdf
description: NPDES compliance evaluation pre-inspection record for the Cadillac WWTP inspection begun September 30 and completed October 4, 2013. It describes a generally well-operated plant while documenting aging infrastructure, deteriorated septage and equalization facilities, and the earlier use of the equalization basin for hauled County Landfill leachate.

name: 2014-10-10 - Cadillac WWTP NPDES CSI-Toxics Pre-Inspection Report.pdf
description: Standalone NPDES CSI-Toxics pre-inspection database export completed October 10, 2014. It independently preserves the equalization-basin and hauled County Landfill leachate history documented in the related eight-page inspection package, and is retained because its file structure and page set are distinct.

name: 2009-11-19 - Cadillac WWTP IPP Reconnaissance Post-Inspection Report.pdf
description: MDEQ post-inspection database export for the November 19, 2009 Cadillac WWTP Industrial Pretreatment Program reconnaissance inspection. The inspector records elevated zinc in biosolids found during September 2009 point-source sampling, identifies Cadillac Castings as the source reported by the plant superintendent, and calls for a compliance report and permit-monitoring revisions.

name: 2026-07-14 - Cadillac Response to Violation Notice VN-019184.pdf
description: Cadillac's signed July 14, 2026 response to EGLE Violation Notice VN-019184. The City attributes the April 16-29 partial tertiary-treatment bypass to snowmelt, frozen ground, flooding and 11.79 inches of April precipitation, asserts that the reportable-discharge-scenario threshold was exceeded, and confirms that future bypasses will be reported. Attachments include a NOAA precipitation table and EGLE's April 22 and April 27 reporting reminders. This record does not show that EGLE accepted the City's weather defense or closed the violation.

name: 2018-06-15 - Cadillac WWTP Compliance Sampling Inspection Final Report.pdf
description: MDEQ's final report for the May 9-10, 2018 compliance sampling inspection at Cadillac WWTP, preserved in the exact 18-page MiEnviro PDF rendition of the June 15 transmittal and attached workbook. It documents a 24-hour composite before disinfection, post-disinfection outfall grabs, an upstream Clam River grab, a reported 1.975 MGD flow and conventional, cyanide and metals results. The report contains no PFAS analytes and is not treated as evidence of PFAS presence, removal or source attribution.

name: 2026-09-02 - EGLE Follow-up to SVN-01952 - Local Limits.pdf
description: EGLE's September 2, 2026 follow-up to Second Violation Notice SVN-01952. WRD finds Cadillac's proposed daily maximum local limits for benzidine (0.6 µg/L), beryllium (17 µg/L) and phenol (1,737 µg/L) approvable, but requires an attorney certification and certified adopted legal authorities by December 31, 2026 before final approval. The letter also states that WRD's review did not include worker-health-and-safety compliance under 40 CFR 403.5(b)(7).
